1000118.etyen:
Internationalism, based on the official name coined by Thomas Sankara and adopted on 4 August 1984. It was formed from Moore burkĩna (“honest, upright; incorruptible”) and Dyula faso (“father's house; fatherland”), and therefore means approximately “land of upright people”. First attested in 1984, when it replaced the former name Øvre Volta (“Upper Volta”).
Parallel international adaptations include Norwegian Nynorsk Burkina Faso, Danish Burkina Faso, Swedish Burkina Faso, German Burkina Faso, Dutch Burkina Faso and English Burkina Faso.

1000630.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Czech Čech (“Czech person”) and the international country-name ending -ia. The Czech ethnonym derives from Old Czech Čech (“Czech person”), from the root čel- (“member of the people, kinsman”) and -ch (“personal-name suffix”), ultimately related to člověk (“human”).
Compare the parallel formations Danish Tjekkiet, Swedish Tjeckien, Dutch Tsjechië, German Tschechien, Russian Чехия (Čexija) and English Czechia.

1001142.etyen:
An archaizing formation after Old Norse sátt f (“reconciliation, covenant, agreement”), from Proto-Germanic *sahtiz f (“reproach; agreement, reconciliation”), from *sakaną (“to charge, dispute”) + *-þiz (“abstract noun suffix”).
The Old Norse noun is cognate with Icelandic sátt and sætt, Faroese sátt and sætt, Old Swedish sāt and sǣt, Old English sæht, English saught and Scots saucht (“agreement, reconciliation; peace”).

1001398.etyen:
Borrowed from Swedish grattis (“congrats, congratulations”), formed from a clipping of gratulera (“to congratulate”) and -is (“familiar suffix”). The underlying verb ultimately derives from Latin grātulārī (“to congratulate”), formed from Latin grātus (“pleasing, welcome; grateful”), from Proto-Italic *gʷrātos (“grateful”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷr̥Htós (“praised”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH- (“to welcome, praise”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk grattis (“congrats, congratulations”) and the related shortening English congrats.

ved (“at, upon”) + sikt (“sight, presentation”) + veksel (“bill of exchange”), literally “at-sight bill of exchange”.
